harvestMonths.region: Eastern South African botanical account — edible flowers only
harvestMonths.notes: These are source flowering months for edible flowers, not a calendar for leaf availability or sowing. Local picking must be recorded separately.

yearsToFirstCrop.notes: No qualified numeric planting-to-first-food age in the checked sources. Record planting date, starting age and actual bearing.

yearsToFullBearing.notes: No measured full-bearing age was established; no yield ramp is inferred.

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: No qualified food kg per plant with age, edible-product basis and management context. Missing output is unknown.

chillUnits.notes: No cultivar-specific numeric chilling requirement verified.

pollination.notes: No source-supported universal pollen classification established.

supplementaryReferences.title: Edible part and local use
supplementaryReferences.quote: both the leaves and flowers can be used in salads and other dishes
supplementaryReferences.note: Leaves and flowers are documented culinary parts. Medicinal bulb use does not make every part a food.

care: It tolerates prolonged drought but grows better with regular water. SANBI records its eastern South African distribution.
purchase: Ask for Tulbaghia violacea, rather than a plant identified only as wild garlic. Record local leaf and flower picking separately.

sourceChecks.observations: Read indexed primary SANBI page content. Direct PlantZAfrica requests in this audit returned HTTP 403; this is not a claim that every individual endpoint was live-tested.

gaps: No numeric leaf yield, first-food age or complete leaf-picking calendar.
